moduleTitle: Module 5. Renal, Digestive, Metabolic, Immune and Reproductive Physiology

competencies.name: Kidney functions
competencies.can: List the homeostatic functions of the kidney including water and electrolyte balance, acid base regulation, waste excretion, blood pressure control, and hormone production.

competencies.name: Nephron structure and function
competencies.can: Match each nephron segment to its dominant transport function and distinguish a cortical from a juxtamedullary nephron by capability.

competencies.name: Three renal processes
competencies.can: Define filtration, reabsorption, secretion, and excretion and write the equation that relates them for any solute.

competencies.name: Filtration membrane and selectivity
competencies.can: Describe the three layers of the filtration membrane and predict which plasma components appear in the filtrate based on size and charge.

competencies.name: Net filtration pressure and GFR
competencies.can: Calculate net filtration pressure from glomerular hydrostatic pressure, capsular pressure, and colloid osmotic pressure and predict the effect of each change on glomerular filtration rate.

competencies.name: Regulation of GFR
competencies.can: Compare myogenic autoregulation, tubuloglomerular feedback, sympathetic control, and hormonal control and predict the effect of afferent and efferent arteriolar constriction on filtration rate.

competencies.name: Renal clearance
competencies.can: Calculate the clearance of a substance and use inulin and creatinine clearance to estimate glomerular filtration rate.

competencies.name: Clearance and handling inference
competencies.can: Use a clearance value relative to glomerular filtration rate to determine whether a substance is net reabsorbed or net secreted.

competencies.name: Proximal tubule reabsorption
competencies.can: Explain how the sodium gradient drives reabsorption of glucose, amino acids, and water in the proximal tubule and state why reabsorption there is described as isosmotic.

competencies.name: Transport maximum and renal threshold
competencies.can: Distinguish transport maximum from renal threshold and explain the appearance of glucose in urine when plasma glucose is elevated.

competencies.name: Tubular secretion
competencies.can: State the purpose of tubular secretion and name substances secreted including hydrogen ion, potassium, and organic anions such as drugs.

competencies.name: Countercurrent mechanism
competencies.can: Explain how the countercurrent multiplier of the loop of Henle and the countercurrent exchanger of the vasa recta build and preserve the medullary osmotic gradient.

competencies.name: Antidiuretic hormone and urine concentration
competencies.can: Trace the response to dehydration from osmoreceptor firing through antidiuretic hormone release to aquaporin insertion and concentrated urine.

competencies.name: Renin angiotensin aldosterone system
competencies.can: Trace the renin angiotensin aldosterone pathway from the stimulus for renin release to the effects of angiotensin II and aldosterone on vessels, tubules, and blood pressure.

competencies.name: Natriuretic peptides
competencies.can: Explain how atrial natriuretic peptide opposes the renin angiotensin aldosterone system and state the stimulus for its release.

competencies.name: Potassium handling
competencies.can: Explain how aldosterone and plasma potassium regulate potassium secretion in the collecting duct and predict the effect of a potassium wasting diuretic.

competencies.name: Micturition
competencies.can: Trace the micturition reflex and explain how the internal and external sphincters allow voluntary control.

competencies.name: Urinalysis
competencies.can: Perform a urinalysis measuring specific gravity, pH, glucose, protein, ketones, and blood and relate any abnormal finding to the renal process that failed.

competencies.name: Renal function calculation
competencies.can: Calculate glomerular filtration rate, clearance, and filtered load from a data set and interpret the values in a clinical case.

competencies.name: Buffer systems
competencies.can: Compare the bicarbonate, phosphate, and protein buffer systems by location and speed and explain why bicarbonate is the dominant extracellular buffer.

competencies.name: Respiratory control of pH
competencies.can: Explain how a change in ventilation shifts the carbon dioxide and bicarbonate equilibrium and therefore plasma pH.

competencies.name: Renal control of pH
competencies.can: Describe how the kidney secretes hydrogen ion and reclaims or generates bicarbonate and explain why renal compensation is slower and more complete than respiratory compensation.

competencies.name: The four acid base disorders
competencies.can: Classify a disorder as respiratory or metabolic and as acidosis or alkalosis from pH, partial pressure of carbon dioxide, and bicarbonate.

competencies.name: Compensation
competencies.can: Determine whether an acid base disorder is uncompensated, partially compensated, or fully compensated and name the system doing the compensating.

competencies.name: Arterial blood gas interpretation
competencies.can: Interpret a set of arterial blood gas values and match the result to a plausible clinical cause.

competencies.name: Volume and osmolarity disturbances
competencies.can: Classify a disturbance as volume depletion or overload and as hypoosmotic, isosmotic, or hyperosmotic and predict the resulting fluid shift between compartments.

competencies.name: Four digestive processes
competencies.can: Distinguish motility, secretion, digestion, and absorption and identify where in the tract each dominates.

competencies.name: Motility patterns
competencies.can: Compare peristalsis, segmentation, and the migrating motor complex by pattern and purpose.

competencies.name: Neural and hormonal regulation
competencies.can: Explain short and long reflex control by the enteric nervous system and match gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin, and glucose dependent insulinotropic peptide to their stimulus and action.

competencies.name: Phases of digestive control
competencies.can: Describe the cephalic, gastric, and intestinal phases and state the dominant control mechanism in each.

competencies.name: Gastric secretion and mucosal protection
competencies.can: Trace the production of hydrochloric acid by the parietal cell and explain how the mucosal barrier protects the stomach and how ulcers develop when it fails.

competencies.name: Pancreatic and biliary secretion
competencies.can: State the components of pancreatic juice and bile and explain how bicarbonate neutralizes chyme and how bile salts emulsify fat.

competencies.name: Carbohydrate and protein digestion and absorption
competencies.can: Trace a starch and a protein from mouth to bloodstream naming the enzymes at each step and the transport mechanism at the brush border.

competencies.name: Lipid digestion and absorption
competencies.can: Trace a triglyceride through emulsification, lipase action, micelle formation, and chylomicron packaging to the lymphatic route and explain why fat takes a different path than glucose.

competencies.name: Liver function and enterohepatic circulation
competencies.can: State the metabolic, storage, and detoxification functions of the liver and trace the enterohepatic circulation of bile salts.

competencies.name: Large intestine and microbiome
competencies.can: Describe water and electrolyte absorption in the colon, the contribution of the microbiome, and the defecation reflex.

competencies.name: Digestive enzyme experiment
competencies.can: Test the effect of pH, temperature, and substrate on a digestive enzyme and relate the results to the region of the tract where that enzyme works.

competencies.name: ATP production pathways
competencies.can: Compare glycolysis, the citric acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation by location, oxygen requirement, and ATP yield.

competencies.name: Absorptive state
competencies.can: Describe the fate of glucose, amino acids, and fats in the absorptive state and identify insulin as the dominant hormone.

competencies.name: Postabsorptive state
competencies.can: Explain how glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and ketogenesis maintain plasma glucose during fasting and name the hormones that drive each.

competencies.name: Integrated glucose regulation
competencies.can: Predict the hormonal and metabolic response to a carbohydrate meal and to a prolonged fast and explain how plasma glucose stays within range in both.

competencies.name: Energy balance and metabolic rate
competencies.can: Define basal metabolic rate, state the factors that raise and lower it, and explain how indirect calorimetry estimates energy expenditure.

competencies.name: Thermoregulation
competencies.can: Trace the negative feedback response to heat and to cold through the hypothalamus and the effectors and explain the mechanism of fever.

competencies.name: Metabolic rate measurement
competencies.can: Estimate metabolic rate from measured or simulated oxygen consumption and compare resting values with values after activity.

competencies.name: Innate defenses
competencies.can: Describe the physical, chemical, and cellular innate defenses and explain what makes them nonspecific and immediate.

competencies.name: Inflammation and fever
competencies.can: Order the events of the inflammatory response and explain how the cardinal signs arise and why fever aids defense.

competencies.name: Adaptive immunity
competencies.can: Compare humoral and cell mediated immunity by the cell responsible, the target, and the mechanism of elimination.

competencies.name: Antibody structure and function
competencies.can: Relate antibody structure to antigen binding and name the mechanisms by which antibodies neutralize or mark a target.

competencies.name: Immune memory and immunization
competencies.can: Compare the primary and secondary antibody responses and explain how active and passive immunization produce protection.

competencies.name: Immune dysfunction
competencies.can: Classify allergy, autoimmunity, and immunodeficiency by what the immune system is doing wrong in each.

competencies.name: Hypothalamic pituitary gonadal axis
competencies.can: Trace the gonadotropin releasing hormone axis to the gonads and place the feedback loops for both sexes.

competencies.name: Male reproductive physiology
competencies.can: Explain the control of spermatogenesis by follicle stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, and testosterone and state the roles of the Sertoli and Leydig cells.

competencies.name: Ovarian cycle
competencies.can: Order the follicular, ovulatory, and luteal phases and explain how the luteinizing hormone surge is triggered by positive feedback.

competencies.name: Uterine cycle
competencies.can: Correlate the menstrual, proliferative, and secretory phases of the uterine cycle with the estrogen and progesterone levels that drive them.

competencies.name: Pregnancy and placental hormones
competencies.can: Explain how human chorionic gonadotropin rescues the corpus luteum and state the roles of placental estrogen, progesterone, and relaxin.

competencies.name: Parturition and lactation
competencies.can: Explain labor as a positive feedback loop driven by oxytocin and compare the hormonal control of milk production with milk ejection.

competencies.name: Hormone cycle graph interpretation
competencies.can: Read a graph of gonadotropin and ovarian hormone levels across a cycle and identify the day of ovulation and the event driving each peak.

competencies.name: Multisystem integration case
competencies.can: Given a clinical scenario, trace the disturbance through at least three organ systems and identify the compensatory responses in the order they occur.

competencies.name: Exercise as an integrated response
competencies.can: Build an integrated account of moderate exercise across the muscular, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, and renal systems.

competencies.name: Drawing based synthesis check
competencies.can: Draw and annotate a homeostatic pathway from memory and explain each step aloud or in writing without notes.
